target: Acabamos de mudarnos a un apartamento nuevo.
english: We just moved to a new apartment.
tip: Acabar = to finish, so Acabamos de mudarnos is literally 'we finish from moving' – Spanish's way of saying 'just did'. Present tense, past meaning.

target: Me duele la oreja derecha desde ayer.
english: My right ear has hurt since yesterday.
tip: Your body isn't 'yours' in Spanish: la oreja, not mi oreja. Me duele already says whose ear hurts – adding mi would sound oddly possessive.

target: Quiero que los niños coman más verdura.
english: I want the kids to eat more vegetables.
tip: Subjunctive after quiero que: coman (not comen).

target: ¿Quieres que te lo lleve a casa?
english: Do you want me to bring it to you at home?
tip: Quieres and lleve have different subjects – that switch forces que + subjunctive. If YOU wanted to bring it, it'd be plain ¿quieres llevarlo?, no que at all.

target: Antes de que anochezca, deberíamos volver al hotel.
english: Before it gets dark, we should return to the hotel.
tip: 'Antes de que' (before) always takes subjunctive – the event hasn't happened yet.

target: ¿Podría enviarme el acta de la reunión anterior, por favor?
english: Could you send me the minutes of the previous meeting, please?
tip: ¿Podría...? is the workplace-safe ask: conditional 'could you' softens the request. Podría enviarme + por favor = polished formal; puedes would sound chummy.

target: Ella estudia para ser abogada.
english: She's studying to be a lawyer.
tip: Para + ser + profession = purpose/goal.

target: Alquilamos un carro por una semana.
english: We rented a car for a week.
tip: "Por una semana" – "por" for duration of time. How long the rental lasted.

target: Le compré un regalo a mi madre.
english: I bought my mother a gift.
tip: Spanish doubles up on purpose: le already means 'to her', yet a mi madre still appears. Not redundant – le is grammar glue, a mi madre the clarifier.

target: Te cambio mi turno por el tuyo.
english: I'll trade you my shift for yours.
tip: "Por" = in exchange for: "Cambié mi coche por uno nuevo." Por for swapping one thing for another.

target: Mis amigos y yo quedamos los viernes.
english: My friends and I meet up on Fridays.
tip: Quedar normally means 'to remain' – but between friends, quedamos = we meet up. Quedamos los viernes is making Friday plans, not staying home.

target: Lo hice por ti, no por mí.
english: I did it for you, not for me.
tip: Por + person = on behalf of, for the sake of.

target: Dale recuerdos a tu madre de mi parte.
english: Give my regards to your mother.
tip: Recuerdos means memories AND greetings: Dale recuerdos = 'give her my regards', the standard warm sign-off. De mi parte ('from my side') makes it personal.

target: Conocí a mi mejor amigo en el colegio.
english: I met my best friend at school.
tip: Preterite flips conocer from 'know' to 'meet': Conocí a mi mejor amigo = I MET him. Knowing is ongoing; the preterite pinpoints the moment it began.

target: Ni que fueras el único que tiene problemas.
english: It's not like you're the only one with problems.
tip: Ni que + past subjunctive = sarcastic 'as if!': Ni que fueras el único = 'it's not like you're the only one'. Literally 'not even if you were'.

target: Por más que estudie, no aprueba el examen.
english: No matter how much she studies, she doesn't pass the exam.
tip: Por más que + subjunctive = no matter how much.

target: Quiero que mis hijos estudien lo que les guste.
english: I want my children to study whatever they like.
tip: Double subjunctive: estudien (after quiero que) and guste (after lo que – 'whatever they like' isn't a known thing yet, so it goes subjunctive too).

target: Me gusta la música.
english: I like music.
tip: "Me" is indirect object – music pleases me.

target: Lo hice por ti.
english: I did it for you.
tip: 'Por ti' = for your sake, because of you. 'Para ti' would mean it's destined to be handed to you. Both translate 'for you' – Spanish makes you pick the why or the where-to.

target: Cuando llegues a casa, llámame.
english: When you get home, call me.
tip: Why not 'llegas'? Future-time cuando takes subjunctive – getting home hasn't happened yet. 'Cuando llegues' = whenever that turns out to be.

target: ¿Habrá sitio en el restaurante?
english: Will there be room at the restaurant?
tip: 'Habrá' is the future of haber – used here for speculation.

target: No te olvides de comprar pan.
english: Don't forget to buy bread.
tip: Affirmative was 'olvídate'; add no and the command flips: the pronoun jumps in front and the verb turns subjunctive – 'no te olvides'.

target: Ponte el abrigo, que hace frío.
english: Put your coat on, it's cold.
tip: Reflexive tú command: "Ponte" = Put on (yourself). Irregular command "pon" + reflexive "te" attached.

target: Para llegar a tiempo, salimos temprano.
english: To arrive on time, we left early.
tip: Para + infinitive for purpose / goal.

target: Acuéstate temprano, mañana hay que madrugar.
english: Go to bed early, we have to get up early tomorrow.
tip: Who must get up? Nobody named: 'hay que' states duty with no subject at all. 'Hay que madrugar' = early rising is required, for whoever's listening.

target: Le pedí un aumento a mi jefe.
english: I asked my boss for a raise.
tip: No 'for' needed: pedir already means 'ask for'. You request the thing directly – 'pedí un aumento' – and the person just takes le/a. 'Pedir por' is a different beast.

target: Si no trabajas aquí, no lo entiendes.
english: If you don't work here, you don't understand.
tip: Surprise: 'si' resists the subjunctive. Real, open conditions take plain present – 'si no trabajas' – never 'si trabajes'. Save subjunctive for unreal ifs.

target: ¿Puedo llamarte más tarde? Estoy ocupado ahora.
english: Can I call you later? I'm busy right now.
tip: ¿Puedo llamarte? isn't really about ability – it's asking permission, just like English 'can I'. Poder does both jobs: capability and polite requests.

target: Cierro la puerta con llave antes de irme.
english: I lock the door before leaving.
tip: Spanish has no everyday verb for 'lock'. You close 'con llave' – with a key. Drop 'con llave' and 'cierro la puerta' is just shutting the door, not locking it.

target: Mi madre siempre me dice que tenga cuidado.
english: My mother always tells me to be careful.
tip: "Que tenga" – subjunctive after "decir que" (telling someone to do something).
